title: Proxy Compression for Language Modeling
claim: Train one model on mixed compressed and raw inputs so a discarded external compressor aids efficiency yet inference stays raw-byte.
layout: 3 regions, left-to-right, dashed boxes separate data preparation, modeling, inference
description: A wide figure split into dashed-border regions. The large left region, Training Data Preparation, starts with a training corpus at the bottom. One arrow, labeled UTF-8, leads to a blue box of raw byte values. Another arrow goes up to a yellow Proxy Compressor box (Tokenization / Neural / Gzip), which outputs a pink box of compressed token IDs. Both feed a central bordered stack of mixed-representation inputs: pink rows wrapped in <comp> tags and blue rows wrapped in <raw> tags, packed together. An arrow leads right to a gray Language Model box in the Modeling region, topped by a small bar chart for next-symbol prediction. Below, a Byte-level Inference region feeds only raw blue bytes up into the model. Pink marks compressed data and blue marks raw bytes.
caption: Overview of proxy compression for language modeling. During training, we prepare mixed-representation inputs by combining compressed sequences with raw UTF-8 bytes, which are packed together to train a single language model with next-symbol prediction over both representations. Different representations are associated with special sentinels, such as ⟨comp⟩, ⟨/comp⟩for compressed data and ⟨raw⟩and ⟨/raw⟩for raw data. At inference time, the proxy compressor is discarded entirely, and the model operates solely on raw bytes. By training primarily on compressed data (e.g., 90% of training data in this work), this approach captures the training efficiency benefits of compressed data without hard-wiring the compressor into the model’s interface.
abstract: Modern language models are trained almost exclusively on token sequences produced by a fixed tokenizer, an external lossless compressor often over UTF-8 byte sequences, thereby coupling the model to that compressor. This work introduces proxy compression, an alternative training scheme that preserves the efficiency benefits of compressed inputs while providing an end-to-end, raw-byte interface at inference time. During training, a single language model is jointly trained on raw byte sequences and compressed views generated by external compressors; through the process, the model learns to internally align compressed sequences and raw bytes. This alignment enables strong transfer between the two formats, even when training predominantly on compressed inputs that are discarded at inference. Extensive experiments on code language modeling demonstrate that proxy compression substantially improves training efficiency and significantly outperforms pure byte-level baselines given fixed compute budgets. As model scale increases, these gains become more pronounced, and proxy-trained models eventually match or surpass tokenizer approaches, all while operating solely on raw bytes and retaining the inherent robustness of byte-level modeling. Our code is available at https://github.com/LZhengisme/proxy-compression.
